task: Finalize this export handoff draft for field coordinators using Wren Map Studio 1.6. The publishing system renders the two marked sections as independently accessible tabs, and coordinators may receive a direct link to either tab. Keep each tab usable on its own and retain the linked reference destinations.
source_facts: Wren Map Studio 1.6 is a synthetic browser-based mapping application. This specification is authoritative for every behavior, label, example, and link destination on this page. The publishing system interprets the exact markers <!-- tab: CSV -->, <!-- tab: GeoJSON -->, and <!-- endtab --> as independently accessible tabs. Either tab can be distributed by direct link without showing the other tab's contents. The audience is field coordinators handing off a published point layer. Both supported export workflows begin in project meadow-survey, on the published point layer hydrants, with the Exporter role. Both use revision h12, which contains 64 features. Draft layers cannot be exported. Both workflows must independently identify the project, layer, role, published-state prerequisite, and revision check. Each tab must independently explain that exports contain the entire published layer rather than the current map selection. The layer's Revision panel displays its published revision. If it is not h12, stop and ask the survey lead which revision to hand off rather than selecting a different revision by guesswork. The Export panel has a Format selector and Download action. For the CSV workflow, select CSV then Download. The output filename is hydrants-h12.csv, encoded as UTF-8, with a header row followed by 64 data rows. CSV columns in order are asset_id, longitude, latitude, and inspection_state. For the GeoJSON workflow, select GeoJSON then Download. The output filename is hydrants-h12.geojson, containing a FeatureCollection with 64 Point features. Each GeoJSON feature has asset_id and inspection_state properties. GeoJSON point coordinates are ordered longitude then latitude. In both formats, coordinates use WGS 84 decimal degrees. The example point is longitude -73.9857 and latitude 40.7484; its CSV row values appear in longitude,latitude order and its GeoJSON coordinates array is [-73.9857, 40.7484]. CSV row counts exclude the header. GeoJSON feature counts refer to elements of the features array, not the number of properties. Recipients needing a spreadsheet use CSV; recipients needing point geometry use GeoJSON. Each workflow finishes by checking the output filename and format-specific count and sending the file with the revision identifier h12 to the recipient. If the count is not 64, stop the handoff and report the filename and observed count to the survey lead. Exports are read-only with respect to the map and do not change the published layer. /docs/wren/coordinates is the valid coordinate-order reference for both tabs. /docs/wren/csv-columns defines the CSV columns. /docs/wren/geojson-properties defines the GeoJSON properties. These three reference destinations are part of the published handoff documentation; the coordinate-order link appears in both independently distributed tabs. Each workflow must remain understandable without following these supplementary links.
draft:
# Hand off the hydrants layer

Choose CSV for a spreadsheet recipient or GeoJSON for a recipient who needs point geometry. The following tabs describe exports in Wren Map Studio 1.6.

<!-- tab: CSV -->
## CSV for spreadsheet recipients

### Confirm the input

Open project **meadow-survey** and the published point layer **hydrants** using the **Exporter** role. Draft layers cannot be exported. In the layer's **Revision** panel, confirm **h12**. If another revision is displayed, stop and ask the survey lead which revision to hand off. Do not guess a replacement revision.

The export contains the entire published layer, regardless of the current map selection. Revision h12 contains 64 features, so selecting a smaller area on the map does not reduce this file to that area. Exporting is read-only and does not change the published layer.

### Download and inspect

Open **Export**, select **CSV** in **Format**, and choose **Download**. The file is named `hydrants-h12.csv`. It uses UTF-8 encoding and has these columns in order:

```text
asset_id,longitude,latitude,inspection_state
```

Coordinates use WGS 84 decimal degrees. Longitude precedes latitude: the example point has longitude `-73.9857` and latitude `40.7484`, so its coordinate values appear as `-73.9857,40.7484` in those two CSV columns.

See the [coordinate-order reference](/docs/wren/coordinates) when mapping columns in another tool, and the [CSV column definitions](/docs/wren/csv-columns) for field descriptions.

### Complete the handoff

Check that the filename is `hydrants-h12.csv` and that the file contains 64 data rows, excluding the header row. If the count differs, stop the handoff and report the filename and observed count to the survey lead. Otherwise, send the file together with revision identifier **h12** so the spreadsheet recipient knows which published input it represents.
<!-- endtab -->

<!-- tab: GeoJSON -->
## GeoJSON for geometry recipients

### Confirm the input

Open project **meadow-survey** and the published point layer **hydrants** using the **Exporter** role. Draft layers cannot be exported. In the layer's **Revision** panel, confirm **h12**. If another revision is displayed, stop and ask the survey lead which revision to hand off. Do not guess a replacement revision.

The export contains the entire published layer, regardless of the current map selection. Revision h12 contains 64 features, so selecting a smaller area on the map does not reduce this file to that area. Exporting is read-only and does not change the published layer.

### Download and inspect

Open **Export**, select **GeoJSON** in **Format**, and choose **Download**. The file is named `hydrants-h12.geojson`. It contains a `FeatureCollection` of `Point` features, each with `asset_id` and `inspection_state` properties.

Coordinates use WGS 84 decimal degrees. Each point's coordinate array is ordered longitude, then latitude. For example, `[-73.9857, 40.7484]` represents longitude -73.9857 and latitude 40.7484.

See the [coordinate-order reference](/docs/wren/coordinates) when importing into another mapping tool, and the [GeoJSON property definitions](/docs/wren/geojson-properties) for the nongeometry fields.

### Complete the handoff

Check that the filename is `hydrants-h12.geojson` and that its `features` array contains 64 elements. Count features, not properties within each feature. If the count differs, stop the handoff and report the filename and observed count to the survey lead. Otherwise, send the file together with revision identifier **h12** so the geometry recipient knows which published input it represents.
<!-- endtab -->
